summary: Strong, well-reasoned PR — the dual-channel stream design and never-reused subscription identity are the right solution to stale order-book packets, all 6 ticket ACs and all 5 Gherkin claims reproduced live (102/102 recipe nodes), lint:tsc clean and 333/333 tests green, and every prior review finding is resolved. One must_fix: the ResizeObserver that backs aria-valuemax and the resize re-clamp never attaches on the cold-load path, so neither behaviour its comment promises actually happens until the user interacts with the divider.

comments.body:
**suggestion** — These two floors make the split unable to fit the popup at all, which clips the order book's value column.

At a 360px viewport the body measures ~338px, while the panes plus divider need `140 + 224 + 2 = 366px`. The `overflow-x` fallback on the body absorbs the difference, so nothing breaks — but the order book's second column is cut off mid-value (`Size (ET…`, truncated numbers) and is only readable by scrolling horizontally.

Measured live at a 360px viewport: `{"viewport":360,"bodyWidth":338,"book":140,"form":224,"askRows":5}` — both panes sit exactly on their floors, so this is structural rather than a rounding artifact, and it will reproduce in the real 360px extension popup.

I don't think this is a bug — the floors and the scroll fallback are deliberate and documented. But the ticket's AC is "works in both compact (mobile popup) and expanded (fullscreen) layouts", and today the ladder's values are unreadable in the compact case without horizontal scrolling, so it's worth a conscious product call rather than being settled by the constants. Options, roughly in increasing effort: lower `ORDER_BOOK_MIN_WIDTH_PX` so both panes fit (the price column alone is narrow), relax the form floor while the book is open, or stack the panel below the form under a width breakpoint.

*nitpick* — The tap-to-prefill wiring is the one seam in this feature without a test that crosses it.

Both halves are covered well individually: `usePerpsOrderForm.test.ts` proves a new `limitPricePrefill` object reference applies (and re-applies after a manual edit), and `order-book.test.tsx` proves a row click calls `onSelectPrice` with the right price. What no test covers is this handler joining them — that clicking an order-book row on the page switches `orderType` to `'limit'` *and* lands the price in `limit-price-input`.

It does work — I verified it live: tapping the `$1,890` ask row switched the form to Limit and set the input to `1890.0`. But it's the exact integration a reviewer asked QA to cover back in July, and it's cheap to assert at the page level now that the panel mounts in `perps-order-entry-page.test.tsx`.
